summary: Frontend-only mobile game testing for the hold-charge-release jump prototype at mobile viewport 390x844. All 6 requested testIDs are present and behave correctly: game-root, score-value, best-value, debug-overlay, charge-surface, game-over-overlay, final-score, final-best, play-again-button, perfect-label. Charge grows to ~100% at ~1.7s hold; releasing launches the blob; scoring/landing works; Game Over overlay shows correctly; Play Again resets score to 0 without a reload; best score persists across reload via AsyncStorage/localStorage (verified localStorage['jumpcharge.bestScore']='3' pre-reload, BEST=1..3 restored post-reload). Two runtime deprecation warnings observed from React Native Web. Gameplay balance is highly unforgiving: the sweet-spot hold duration to consistently score is a narrow ~600-700ms band; full-charge (1.7s) overshoots every platform and drops the blob to Game Over on the first jump, contradicting the assumption in the request that ~0.7-1.0s reliably scores.

issues: Difficulty tuning: With CONFIG.maxJumpVX=640 / maxJumpVY=1480 vs. minPlatformDistance=150 / maxPlatformDistance=340 (easy=150..220 for first 3), holds >~750ms already overshoot and holds <~600ms fall short. Sweet-spot band is <150ms wide. Recommend either (a) increasing minJumpVX to ~320 or (b) narrowing charge->velocity mapping so mid-charge reliably lands. The agent-to-agent note said 0.7-1.0s should score but 700-1000ms holds also caused Game Over in testing.

First full-charge (1.7s) hold always causes Game Over: the blob flies past all initially-generated 'easy' platforms and falls into the abyss. This is the exact scenario a new user is guided into by the 'Hold to charge · Release to jump' hint plus the visible charge bar filling.

react_native_issues.issue: Uses deprecated shadow* props (shadowColor, shadowOpacity, shadowRadius, shadowOffset). React Native Web logs: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".'. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:766-769

React Native Web logs 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' for several Animated.View / View components (hint, burst, blob, hud, perfect-wrap, debug overlay). Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:429, 437, 457, 473, 487, 498, 505, 514

action_items: Re-tune jump physics or platform spacing so a full 100% charge is REACHABLE but not always fatal (currently max charge always overshoots). Consider lowering CONFIG.maxJumpVX to ~520 and/or bumping CONFIG.maxPlatformDistance so the max jump can still land somewhere. Alternatively increase easy-start forgiveness.

Fix widen the playable hold window at the low end: raise CONFIG.minJumpVX (e.g. 300-330) so even short taps clear the min gap, letting users progressively learn charge timing without instant Game Over.

Migrate deprecated RN-Web props: replace shadow* with boxShadow (or wrap behind Platform.select), and move pointerEvents='none' from prop to style.pointerEvents on the affected Animated.View / View elements in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx.

(Optional) Move `import { storage } from '@/src/utils/storage'` to top-of-file instead of dynamic import inside onGameOver and useEffect; the dynamic import adds ~1-2s of tail latency before the best score persists on web (during that window a hard reload loses the write).
critical_code_review_comments: Best-score persistence uses `import('@/src/utils/storage').then(({storage}) => storage.setItem(...))` inside a `setBest(prev => ...)` reducer. Reducers should be pure — side effects (dynamic import + async write) inside them may run twice in React Strict Mode. Move the persistence side effect out to `useEffect(() => storage.setItem(BEST_SCORE_KEY, best), [best])` and use a static top-level import for storage.

`platforms` is a shared value holding a plain array reassigned each frame; the code correctly avoids in-place mutation, but the `any[]` typing is loose. Consider a small `Platform` interface for safety.
`onPressIn` / `onPressOut` are wrapped with `useCallback([])` while reading many shared values; that's fine, but the eslint-disable comments hide missing deps that could bite when refactored.
`initWorld` snapshot depends on window size (W,H); when the browser is resized mid-game there is no re-init path — camera anchors go stale.
seed_data_creation: Set window.localStorage['jumpcharge.bestScore'] directly (as '5') to verify the read path independently of gameplay; cleared before each run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use mobile viewport 390x844. To reliably score, hold roughly 620-720ms (charge ~36-42%). Holds <600ms fall short; holds >~800ms consistently overshoot on the first few platforms and cause Game Over. Wait at least 2s after Game Over before reloading to observe best-score persistence (AsyncStorage write via dynamic import is slow on web). All required testIDs exist: game-root, charge-surface, score-value, best-value, debug-overlay, game-over-overlay, play-again-button, final-score, final-best.
rca_of_issue: Difficulty spike: at 100% charge vx=640, vy=1480, so airtime = 2*1480/2600 ≈ 1.14s and horizontal reach ≈ 728px. The first three 'easy' platforms only span 150-220px apart, so a full-charge jump flies over every platform in the initial spawn window and eventually reaches y > camY+H triggering DEAD/Game Over. Simultaneously at 0% charge vx=250, vy=720, airtime ≈ 0.55s, reach ≈ 138px, which is under the 150 minimum gap — so a bare tap can never clear the first gap either. The playable band is narrow. The persistence 'bug' initially observed was actually a timing artifact — the dynamic `import('@/src/utils/storage')` + AsyncStorage.setItem finishes ~1-2s after `onGameOver`, and an immediate reload cut the write off. With ≥2s wait, best persists correctly across reloads.
